meta.title: Pain001 Technical Reference: CLI, Python API and REST
meta.description: Complete reference for pain001 v0.0.57 — CLI subcommands and flags, Python API, REST endpoints under /api/v1, scheme rulebooks, input normalisation, and plugin architecture.
meta.deck: Every flag, endpoint, and behaviour of pain001 v0.0.57 — taken from the shipped code, not from aspiration.

text.This reference documents the command-lin: This reference documents the command-line interface, Python API, REST microservice, and validation pipeline for pain001 v0.0.57. Every flag, endpoint, and behaviour listed here is taken from the shipped code, not from aspiration.
text.Pain001 supports <strong>11 ISO 20022 me: Pain001 supports 11 ISO 20022 message definitions: pain.001.001.03 through pain.001.001.12 (Customer Credit Transfer Initiation, ten versions) and pain.008.001.02 (Customer Direct Debit Initiation).
text.1. Command-Line Interface<a class=\"head: 1. Command-Line Interface#
text.The <code>pain001</code> executable grou: The pain001 executable groups its functionality into subcommands. Running it with only generation flags invokes generate implicitly, so existing automation keeps working.
text.Convert a data file into schema-validate: Convert a data file into schema-validated ISO 20022 XML (default command).
Validate input data without writing XML.
text.Show the required and optional fields fo: Show the required and optional fields for a message type.
text.Scaffold a starter CSV template for a me: Scaffold a starter CSV template for a message type.
text.Launch the FastAPI REST microservice (re: Launch the FastAPI REST microservice (requires the api extra).
text.Launch the in-tree Model Context Protoco: Launch the in-tree Model Context Protocol server (5 tools; the full 17-tool server ships as pain001-mcp).
text.Inspect and manage discovered loader, va: Inspect and manage discovered loader, validator, scheme, and writer plugins.
text.Directory that receives the generated XM: Directory that receives the generated XML.
text.Override the bundled Jinja2 template or: Override the bundled Jinja2 template or XSD schema.
text.Load defaults from a configuration profi: Load defaults from a configuration profile (--profile, --show-config).
text.Validate input against the JSON Schema,: Validate input against the JSON Schema, XSD, and scheme rulebook without writing output.
text.Report each scheme rule that passed or f: Report each scheme rule that passed or failed, human- or machine-readable.
text.Memory-bounded chunked processing for la: Memory-bounded chunked processing for large batches (default 1,000 transactions per chunk; each chunk becomes its own XML file with recomputed NbOfTxs and CtrlSum).
text.Emit machine-readable run metrics for ob: Emit machine-readable run metrics for observability pipelines.
text.Exit codes are CI-friendly: <code>0</cod: Exit codes are CI-friendly: 0 success, 1 validation failure, 2 usage error.
text.2. Python API<a class=\"heading-anchor\": 2. Python API#
text.Every generated document passes three la: Every generated document passes three layers before it is written:
text.<strong>Input validation</strong> — each: Input validation — each record is checked against the message type's JSON Schema, with field-alias normalisation and IBAN/BIC syntax checks.
text.<strong>Scheme rulebook</strong> (option: Scheme rulebook (optional) — SEPA SCT, SEPA Instant, SEPA SDD Core, SEPA B2B, or cross-border credit transfer rules.
text.<strong>XSD validation</strong> — the re: XSD validation — the rendered XML is validated against the official ISO 20022 schema via xmlschema before a single byte is written to disk.
text.Monetary amounts are handled as <code>de: Monetary amounts are handled as decimal.Decimal during XML generation and scheme validation — never IEEE 754 floats — and NbOfTxs / CtrlSum control totals are recomputed from the validated records rather than trusted from input.
text.Beyond pain.001 generation, the core lib: Beyond pain.001 generation, the core library also ships a pain.002 status-report parser and generator (so you can read the bank's accept/reject response) and a camt.053 statement parser and generator for end-of-day reconciliation, plus a VersionMapper that migrates records between message versions.
text.3. REST Microservice<a class=\"heading-a: 3. REST Microservice#
text.All endpoints are mounted under <code>/a: All endpoints are mounted under /api/v1 (with an unversioned /api alias):
text.Queue a large batch for background gener: Queue a large batch for background generation.
text.Interactive documentation is served at <: Interactive documentation is served at /api/docs (Swagger UI), /api/redoc, and /api/reference (Scalar), with the OpenAPI document at /openapi.json.
text.4. Input Normalisation<a class=\"heading: 4. Input Normalisation#
text.Pain001 coerces real-world exports into: Pain001 coerces real-world exports into valid records before validation:
text.<strong>Field aliases</strong> — common: Field aliases — common ERP column names map onto canonical fields (for example amount → payment_amount).
text.<strong>IBAN / BIC normalisation</strong: IBAN / BIC normalisation — whitespace stripped, case folded, then checked (ISO 13616 mod-97 for IBANs, ISO 9362 structure for BICs).
text.<strong>Amounts</strong> — routed throug: Amounts — routed through decimal.Decimal; malformed amounts fail validation instead of silently rounding.
text.<strong>Character set</strong> — transli: Character set — transliteration helpers reduce content to the ISO 20022 Latin character set accepted by SWIFT and SEPA.
text.5. Plugin Architecture<a class=\"heading: 5. Plugin Architecture#
text.The suite is extensible through four ent: The suite is extensible through four entry-point groups: pain001.loaders, pain001.validators, pain001.schemes, and pain001.writers. pain001-loader-xlsx registers through this mechanism and is auto-discovered on install; pain001-loader-mt101 is a standalone parsing library consumed directly (and by the MCP server's convert_mt101 tool). A kill switch — PAIN001_DISABLE_PLUGINS=1 — disables third-party plugin discovery entirely in locked-down environments.
text.6. Quality Gates<a class=\"heading-ancho: 6. Quality Gates#
text.The core library is developed against st: The core library is developed against strict, verifiable gates: 100% line and branch coverage enforced in CI (--cov-fail-under=100), strict mypy typing, 100% docstring coverage, and security linting (Bandit, pip-audit). A CycloneDX SBOM is generated for every release build.
text.Continue with the <a href=\"/installatio: Continue with the Installation Guide, the MCP server for AI agents, or the payments glossary.

meta.title: Pain001 FAQs for Treasury, Ops, Engineering and Audit
meta.description: Why banks reject payment files, pain.001 vs pain.008, the November 2026 deadlines, streaming large batches, security posture, and audit reproducibility — answered plainly.
meta.deck: Straight answers for treasurers, payment operations, engineers, and auditors — phrased the way people actually ask.

text.Straight answers for treasurers, payment: Straight answers for treasurers, payment operations, engineers, and auditors. Questions are phrased the way people actually ask them. For deeper technical detail, see the Technical Reference.
text.For treasury and finance leaders<a class: For treasury and finance leaders#
text.<code>pain.001</code> is the ISO 20022 m: pain.001 is the ISO 20022 message a customer sends to its bank to initiate credit transfers — the XML successor to formats like SWIFT MT101 and domestic flat files. Your bank validates it against a schema and a scheme rulebook before accepting it. Pain001 (the software) produces those files from the data you already have and proves they are valid before you submit them.
text.<strong>What is the difference between p: What is the difference between pain.001 and pain.008?
text.Direction of the pull. <code>pain.001</c: Direction of the pull. pain.001 initiates credit transfers — you push money out. pain.008 initiates direct debits — you collect money owed to you under a mandate. Pain001 generates both: ten versions of pain.001 (.001.03 through .001.12) and pain.008.001.02.
text.<strong>We still send MT101 files. How u: We still send MT101 files. How urgent is migration?
text.Urgent. SWIFT retired MT category 1, 2 a: Urgent. SWIFT retired MT category 1, 2 and 9 messages for cross-border interbank payment instructions in November 2025; corporate channels that still accept MT do so at each bank's discretion and on borrowed time. The MT101 loader converts existing MT101 flows to validated pain.001 without re-keying anything.
text.<strong>What does the November 2026 stru: What does the November 2026 structured address deadline mean for us?
text.From the end of November 2026, fully uns: From the end of November 2026, fully unstructured postal addresses are no longer accepted in CBPR+ cross-border payments; addresses must be structured or hybrid — discrete elements such as town () and country () instead of free-text lines. If your master data holds addresses as blobs, the work is in your data, not your bank connection. Start there. The 2026 briefing covers the timeline in detail.
text.Nothing. The core is dual-licensed Apach: Nothing. The core is dual-licensed Apache-2.0 / MIT; companion packages are Apache-2.0. Commercial use, modification, and redistribution are all permitted. For scale reference, SWIFT's translation SDK alone lists at €10,000–30,000 per year.
text.For payment operations<a class=\"heading: For payment operations#
text.Four recurring causes: schema violations: Four recurring causes: schema violations (wrong element, wrong version, wrong namespace), bad identifiers (IBAN checksum failures, malformed BICs), broken control totals (NbOfTxs / CtrlSum not matching the transactions), and characters outside the ISO 20022 Latin set. Pain001 checks all four before a file exists: JSON Schema validation per record, mod-97 IBAN and ISO 9362 BIC checks, recomputed control totals, charset transliteration, and final XSD validation of the rendered XML.
text.<strong>Can we validate a file without g: Can we validate a file without generating anything?
text.Yes — <code>pain001 --dry-run</code> (or: Yes — pain001 --dry-run (or the validate subcommand, or POST /api/v1/validate). Exit code 0 means valid; 1 means validation failed with field-level errors. Wire it into CI or a pre-submission checklist.
text.Five scheme rulebooks ship built-in: SEP: Five scheme rulebooks ship built-in: SEPA Credit Transfer (sepa-sct), SEPA Instant (sepa-inst), SEPA Direct Debit Core (sepa-sdd), SEPA B2B (sepa-b2b), and cross-border credit transfer (xborder-ct). Use --scheme --explain to see every rule that passed or failed.
text.<strong>Our data lives in Excel. What is: Our data lives in Excel. What is the catch?
text.Excel silently coerces IBAN-like strings: Excel silently coerces IBAN-like strings into numbers. The Excel loader reads .xlsx/.xlsm directly and hard-stops if IBAN columns contain numeric cells — the corruption is caught at load, not at the bank.
text.<code>--streaming</code> processes input: --streaming processes input in memory-bounded chunks (default 1,000 transactions), each emitted as its own XML file with correct recomputed control totals. The REST API offers POST /api/v1/generate/async with job polling for the same reason.
text.For engineers and architects<a class=\"h: For engineers and architects#
text.<strong>How do we integrate it — library: How do we integrate it — library, CLI, or API?
text.All three exist as first-class surfaces:: All three exist as first-class surfaces: a typed Python API, a CLI with CI-friendly exit codes, and a FastAPI microservice (pain001 serve) with sync, async-job, health, and Prometheus metrics endpoints. Same validation pipeline underneath, so results never diverge between surfaces.
text.<strong>Is the XML generation actually s: Is the XML generation actually safe against float rounding?
text.Amounts are <code>decimal.Decimal</code>: Amounts are decimal.Decimal end-to-end in generation and scheme validation — parsed as exact decimals, summed as exact decimals, rendered without float representation. Control totals are recomputed from validated records, never trusted from input.
text.All XML parsing routes through <code>def: All XML parsing routes through defusedxml (blocking XXE and entity-expansion attacks); there is no lxml in the dependency tree. Inputs pass a path-traversal validator. The Docker image runs non-root. A CycloneDX SBOM is generated for core releases, and third-party plugin discovery can be disabled outright with PAIN001_DISABLE_PLUGINS=1.
text.100% line and branch coverage as a hard: 100% line and branch coverage as a hard CI gate on the core (verifiably: 3,828 lines, 926 branches at 100%), strict mypy, 100% docstring coverage, Bandit and pip-audit security linting, and CodeQL scanning. The companion packages carry the same 100% coverage discipline.
text.<strong>Can we extend it for a proprieta: Can we extend it for a proprietary format?
text.Yes — four plugin entry-point groups (<c: Yes — four plugin entry-point groups (pain001.loaders, pain001.validators, pain001.schemes, pain001.writers). The Excel loader is itself a plugin using the public protocol, so it doubles as a reference implementation.
text.For auditors and compliance<a class=\"he: For auditors and compliance#
text.<strong>Can we reproduce a file that was: Can we reproduce a file that was generated last quarter?
text.Yes. Pin the package version, replay the: Yes. Pin the package version, replay the same input, and the output is deterministic. Because the toolchain is open source, the audit trail extends into the code path itself — not just a vendor attestation.
text.No. Every component — CLI, library, REST: No. Every component — CLI, library, REST API, MCP server, LSP — executes locally. There is no telemetry, no SaaS callback, no external validation service. The MCP server speaks stdio only and all 17 of its tools are annotated read-only and idempotent.
text.<a href=\"https://sebastienrousseau.com\: Sebastien Rousseau, a London-based fintech engineering leader, with community contributors. Development is public on GitHub, releases are published to PyPI, and the changelog is versioned with every release.

meta.title: Install Pain001: pip, Docker and First Validated File
meta.description: Install the Pain001 suite on Python 3.10–3.12 via pip or Docker, add Excel and MT101 loaders, and produce your first bank-ready pain.001 file in three commands.
meta.deck: Python 3.10–3.12, pip or Docker, and a validated payment file in three commands.

text.Pain001 runs on <strong>Python 3.10, 3.1: Pain001 runs on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 (each version tested in CI) on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Install what you need; every optional capability is an extra, so the base install stays lean.
text.01. PyPI<a class=\"heading-anchor\" href: 01. PyPI#
text.Redis-backed async job queue for the API: Redis-backed async job queue for the API
text.Companion packages install separately an: Companion packages install separately and are versioned independently:
text.Verify the install and explore the messa: Verify the install and explore the message catalogue:
text.02. Docker<a class=\"heading-anchor\" hr: 02. Docker#
text.Multi-architecture images (<code>linux/a: Multi-architecture images (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) are published to GitHub Container Registry. The container runs as a dedicated non-root user.
text.03. Locked-down environments<a class=\"h: 03. Locked-down environments#
text.Bank and treasury environments often pro: Bank and treasury environments often prohibit dynamic plugin loading. Two controls exist for exactly that case:
text.<code>PAIN001_DISABLE_PLUGINS=1</code> d: PAIN001_DISABLE_PLUGINS=1 disables all third-party plugin discovery; only bundled loaders run.
text.<code>pain001 plugins list</code> / <cod: pain001 plugins list / pain001 plugins show make every discovered plugin auditable before first use.
text.Everything executes locally. No package: Everything executes locally. No package in the suite phones home, calls a SaaS API, or moves payment data off the host.
text.04. First file in three commands<a class: 04. First file in three commands#
text.<code>--dry-run</code> validates against: --dry-run validates against the JSON Schema, the XSD, and (with --scheme) a SEPA or cross-border rulebook without writing output — exit code 0 means the file passed those checks: the schema, and the scheme rulebook where selected. Your bank's own profile and channel rules are separate, and still require bank testing. Drop --dry-run to write the XML.
text.Continue to the <a href=\"/documentation: Continue to the Technical Reference for every flag and endpoint, or the Quickstart FAQ for operational questions.

meta.title: ISO 20022 Payments Glossary in Plain English
meta.description: pain.001, pacs.008, camt.053, CBPR+, VoP, UETR, hybrid addresses, control sums — the payments vocabulary defined for treasurers and operations teams, not just developers.
meta.deck: The payments vocabulary in plain English — for the people who sign off on files, not just the people who generate them.

text.Plain-English definitions of the terms t: Plain-English definitions of the terms that appear across this site and in your bank's channel documentation. Written for treasurers and operations teams first, engineers second.
text.Messages<a class=\"heading-anchor\" href: Messages#
text.<strong>pain.001 — Customer Credit Trans: pain.001 — Customer Credit Transfer Initiation. The XML message a customer sends its bank to order one or more credit transfers. The "pain" family is payment initiation; .001 is the message number; the trailing version (.001.09) pins the schema.
text.<strong>pain.002 — Customer Payment Stat: pain.002 — Customer Payment Status Report. The bank's answer to your pain.001 or pain.008: accepted, partially accepted, or rejected, with ISO reason codes per transaction.
text.<strong>pain.008 — Customer Direct Debit: pain.008 — Customer Direct Debit Initiation. The collection-side twin of pain.001: you pull funds owed to you under a mandate rather than pushing funds out.
text.<strong>pacs.008 / pacs.009.</strong> Th: pacs.008 / pacs.009. The interbank settlement messages your instruction becomes once the bank accepts it. Corporates never author these; banks exchange them.
text.<strong>camt.052 / camt.053 / camt.054.<: camt.052 / camt.053 / camt.054. Account reporting: intraday report, end-of-day statement, and debit/credit notification respectively. camt.053 is what reconciliation teams consume each morning.
text.<strong>MT101.</strong> The legacy SWIFT: MT101. The legacy SWIFT "Request for Transfer" text message that pain.001 replaces. The interbank MT101 relay is decommissioned on 14 November 2026 in favour of pain.001.001.09; corporate-to-bank MT101 persists only at each bank's discretion.
text.Schemes and rulebooks<a class=\"heading-: Schemes and rulebooks#
text.<strong>SEPA SCT / SCT Inst.</strong> Th: SEPA SCT / SCT Inst. The euro credit-transfer schemes (standard and instant) governed by the European Payments Council rulebooks. Instant transfers settle in seconds, around the clock.
text.<strong>SEPA SDD Core / B2B.</strong> Th: SEPA SDD Core / B2B. The euro direct-debit schemes — Core for consumers (with refund rights), B2B for businesses (no refund right, stricter mandate checks).
text.<strong>CBPR+.</strong> Cross-Border Pay: CBPR+. Cross-Border Payments and Reporting Plus: the usage guidelines that profile ISO 20022 messages for SWIFT correspondent banking. When people say "the SWIFT ISO 20022 migration", they mean CBPR+.
text.<strong>HVPS+.</strong> The equivalent p: HVPS+. The equivalent profiling for high-value payment systems (T2, CHAPS, Fedwire and peers).
text.<strong>CGI-MP.</strong> Common Global I: CGI-MP. Common Global Implementation — Market Practice: the group harmonising how corporates use pain messages across banks, so one file format can serve many banking partners.
text.<strong>Verification of Payee (VoP).</st: Verification of Payee (VoP). The EU-mandated name/IBAN match check applied to all SEPA credit transfers since 9 October 2025. Done by the PSP at execution time; clean creditor data determines whether it matches.
text.Identifiers and data<a class=\"heading-a: Identifiers and data#
text.<strong>IBAN.</strong> International Ban: IBAN. International Bank Account Number (ISO 13616), self-checking via a mod-97 checksum — which is why a single transposed digit is detectable before submission.
text.<strong>BIC / BICFI.</strong> The ISO 93: BIC / BICFI. The ISO 9362 Business Identifier Code of a financial institution. The XML element is in pain.001.001.03 but from version 9 — a rename that causes real-world rejections during version upgrades.
text.<strong>LEI.</strong> Legal Entity Ident: LEI. Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442) — the 20-character global company identifier. Over 3 million are active, and regulators increasingly mandate them in payments.
text.<strong>UETR.</strong> Unique End-to-end: UETR. Unique End-to-end Transaction Reference — the UUID that lets a payment be traced across the correspondent chain (SWIFT gpi).
text.<strong>Structured / hybrid address.</st: Structured / hybrid address. Postal addresses as discrete XML elements (street, town, postcode, country) versus free-text lines. From 14 November 2026, CBPR+ rejects fully unstructured addresses; hybrid — structured town and country plus up to two 70-character address lines — remains valid.
text.<strong>NbOfTxs / CtrlSum.</strong> The: NbOfTxs / CtrlSum. The group-header control totals: transaction count and amount sum. Banks recompute them; if yours disagree, the file bounces. Pain001 always derives them from the validated records.
text.<strong>Charge bearer.</strong> Who pays: Charge bearer. Who pays the fees: DEBT (sender), CRED (receiver), SHAR (shared), SLEV (per scheme rules). Legacy MT OUR/BEN/SHA map to the first three.
text.<strong>Remittance information.</strong>: Remittance information. The "what this payment is for" field — free text (140 characters) or structured references. The thing reconciliation teams wish everyone filled in properly.
text.Tooling terms used on this site<a class=: Tooling terms used on this site#
text.<strong>XSD validation.</strong> Checkin: XSD validation. Checking XML against the official ISO 20022 schema definition. Pain001 treats it as a hard gate before any file is written.
text.<strong>MCP — Model Context Protocol.</s: MCP — Model Context Protocol. The open standard through which AI assistants call external tools. pain001-mcp exposes 17 payment tools to any MCP client, locally over stdio.
text.<strong>LSP — Language Server Protocol.<: LSP — Language Server Protocol. The editor-integration standard behind IDE diagnostics. pain001-lsp uses it to validate payment files as you type.
text.<strong>SBOM.</strong> Software Bill of: SBOM. Software Bill of Materials — a machine-readable inventory of every dependency in a release, generated in CycloneDX format for Pain001 core releases.
text.Something missing? <a href=\"https://git: Something missing? Suggest a term — this glossary grows with the questions people actually ask.
